title: Specify prompt-set sampling matrix and A/B criteria for Optimize
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Create a clear, operational spec for how Optimize evaluates model changes: define a prompt-set sampling matrix, per-metric regression thresholds, A/B success criteria, and automated rollback triggers. This ticket will produce acceptance criteria, measurement queries, and a lightweight playbook to hand to SRE/QA for implementation and to Growth for A/B coordination.
context: Recent customer incidents and internal experiments show a gap between our evaluation artifacts (dense prompt sets) and production traffic distribution. Engineering needs deterministic pass/fail rules to automate canary-to-rollout transitions and to trigger rollbacks without manual triage. This work complements prior PRDs on eval gating but focuses on sampling strategy and explicit A/B thresholds appropriate for Optimize workloads (generation quality + unit cost).
scope_inclusions:
- Sampling matrix mapping production traffic slices (intent buckets, token length, top-k/top-p settings) to prompt-set subsets.
- Per-metric baseline definitions and regression thresholds (BLEU/ROUGE variants where applicable, embedding-similarity, hallucination rate, safety flags, latency, cost per 1k tokens).
- A/B test success criteria (primary and secondary metrics, minimum sample size, minimum detectable effect).
- Automated rollback triggers for severe regressions and escalation paths.
- Acceptance criteria and monitoring queries for Console dashboards and alerts.
scope_exclusions:
- Building the full A/B experimentation framework (this ticket defines the spec and measurement queries; implementation will be a follow-up).
- Long-form human eval instrumentation (we only define when/where human evals are required and the sampling for them).
requirements:
1) Sampling matrix: map at least 6 production slices -> prompt-set partitions; include weighting and randomization strategy.
2) Metrics: list final metric names, computation windows, and baseline values (30-day rolling).
3) Regression thresholds: specify soft and hard thresholds per metric, with examples.
4) A/B criteria: define primary metric, MDE, min duration, and risk-adjusted success rule.
5) Rollback triggers: enumerate conditions that cause automatic rollback vs. immediate page.
6) Measurement artifacts: SQL/ClickHouse queries or PromQL snippets for each metric and a dashboard wireframe.
7) Acceptance tests: synthetic runbook that SRE/QA can follow to verify gating works in staging.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sampling matrix defined and approved by ML Research and Growth; includes mapping for intent, token-length buckets, and feature flags.
- For each metric, a baseline and two thresholds documented: soft (warning) and hard (rollback).
- A/B test spec includes: primary metric (embedding-similarity for reranking; quality score composite for generation), MDE (5% relative for primary metric unless justified), min sample size calculation, and min runtime (48 hours or 100k impressions, whichever is larger).
- Automated rollback rules documented: hard threshold breach for primary metric over a 1-hour rolling window triggers rollback; any safety-flag spike above 0.5% triggers immediate halt and paging.
- Measurement queries validated against a 14-day historical window and produce expected baselines.
- PRD + playbook reviewed and approved in stakeholder review with signoffs from ML Research, SRE, Growth, and Legal (if safety thresholds touch policy).
metrics_and_thresholds:
- Quality composite (weighted: 0.6 human-like scoring proxy, 0.3 factuality/QA, 0.1 safety): baseline=0.87; soft threshold = -2% relative; hard threshold = -5% relative.
- Embedding-similarity (cosine) on rerank: baseline=0.79; soft=-3%; hard=-7%.
- Hallucination rate (auto-detected): baseline=0.9% absolute; soft=+0.5pp; hard=+2.0pp.
- Safety flags (policy classifier): baseline=0.12%; soft=+0.3pp; hard=+0.5pp (page on hard).
- Median P95 latency: baseline=210ms; soft=+50ms; hard=+120ms.
- Cost per 1k tokens: baseline=$1.08; soft=+10% relative; hard=+25% relative.
sampling_matrix_summary:
- Slice A: High-frequency intents (search/qa) -> 40% of test set (stratified by prompt templates).
- Slice B: Long-form generation (>512 tokens) -> 15%.
- Slice C: Short completions (<50 tokens) -> 15%.
- Slice D: Low-frequency/edge intents (support workflows) -> 10%.
- Slice E: Safety-sensitive content (policy heuristics) -> 10% (oversampled 3x for human eval triggers).
- Slice F: Canary flag / experimental features -> 10% (route to separate cohort).
Weighting and randomization: deterministic hashing on user-id + timestamp with daily re-seeding in staging; sample allocation is configurable via Optimize Console.
a_b_spec_summary:
Primary metric: quality composite for generation; Secondary: latency and cost.
MDE: 5% relative on primary metric (unless traffic slice justification provided).
Min runtime: 48 hours OR 100k impressions per cohort.
Success rule: primary metric improvement > MDE AND no hard-threshold breaches on safety/latency/cost for both cohorts.
If primary effect is within [MDE, 2*MDE], apply manual review before rollout.
rollback_triggers:
1) Hard threshold breach on primary metric sustained for >1 hour -> auto-rollback to previous model variant.
2) Safety flags exceed hard threshold in any 60-minute window -> immediate halt + page SOC and Product.
3) Latency P95 > hard threshold for >30 minutes affecting >=50% of requests -> rollback.
4) Cost per 1k tokens exceeds hard threshold AND traffic impact >10% -> pause rollout and notify Engineering.
5) Composite alert: two or more soft-thresholds breached simultaneously for >3 hours -> send warning and require go/no-go from PM + ML Research.

decision_log:
- 2026-02-27: Agreed on composite primary metric to capture quality tradeoffs across generation tasks.
- 2026-03-03: Set MDE default to 5% relative; exceptions require documented justification.
- 2026-03-08: Adopted automated rollback on 1-hour hard breaches for primary metric.
- 2026-03-11: Finalized sampling matrix weights after ML Research and Growth signoff.
open_questions:
- Should human-in-the-loop evaluation be required for all safety-sensitive slices before rollout? (proposal: yes for hard-threshold-adjacent changes).
- Do we want separate MDEs per traffic slice by default? (proposal: default MDE, but allow slice-specific overrides).
- Who owns operationalizing the SQL/PromQL snippets into alerting rules? (SRE recommended; PM to coordinate).
